newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 2.

text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Friday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) ministerial confab to adopt resolutions calling for lifting ban on various economic restrictions.
-- Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto should be given more power to manage crises in the report released by the Administrative Reform Council.
-- Hashimoto cabinet's support rate recovers to 44.9 percent according to poll.
-- Poll says 56 percent of public approve consumption tax increase.
-- Japanese Ambassador to Peru Morihisa Aoki says he is waiting for government decision on whether he will keep his ambassadorial post in Peru.
-- A four-month-old baby girl leaves hospital after heart operation without blood transfusion.
-- Nomura Securities Co Ltd had more than 200 present and former high-ranking bureaucrats in its VIP client accounts.
-- More than 40 percent of doctors fail to report on side effects after using special drugs to treat hard-to-cure diseases.
